questions.question: How does the Spring Security filter chain work, and how do you configure it in Spring Security 6?
questions.title: Spring Security Filter Chain and SecurityFilterChain Configuration
questions.direct_answer: Spring Security is built as a **chain of servlet filters** (`FilterChainProxy`) that intercepts every request to handle authentication, authorization, CSRF, CORS, headers, and exception translation. In **Spring Security 6**, you configure it by defining one or more **`SecurityFilterChain` beans** — each mapping URL patterns (`securityMatcher`) to a filter chain. **`WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` was removed in 6.0**; use the **component-based lambda DSL**. Order matters: chains evaluated top-to-bottom, **first match wins**; use **`@Order`** for multiple chains (e.g., `/api/**` JWT + `/web/**` session). Built-in filters cover CSRF, sessions, exceptions, anonymous, auth processing, and authorization; insert custom filters with **`addFilterBefore/After/At`**.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using deprecated WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter; mis-ordering filter chains; confusing authenticationManager setup

sections.title: How Spring Security Plugs Into the Web Stack
sections.content:
At boot time, Spring Security registers a single servlet filter, **`DelegatingFilterProxy`**, which delegates to a Spring-managed bean called **`FilterChainProxy`**. This bean holds one or more **`SecurityFilterChain`** instances.

Each `SecurityFilterChain` is a list of filters applied to requests matching a **`SecurityMatcher`** (URL pattern, HTTP method, etc.).
- For each request, Spring finds the **first matching chain** and runs its filters in order.
- Every request passes through this chain **before** hitting your `@RestController`.
- The chain decides whether to let it through, reject it, or redirect to login.

**For reactive WebFlux**, the equivalent is `SecurityWebFilterChain` with analogous filters.

sections.title: Filter Chain Order (Servlet)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    req["HTTP request"] --> dfp["DelegatingFilterProxy"]
    dfp --> fcp["FilterChainProxy (Spring managed)"]
    fcp --> match{"SecurityMatcher: which chain?"}
    match --> chain["Selected SecurityFilterChain"]
    chain --> f1["DisableEncodeUrlFilter"]
    f1 --> f2["WebAsyncManagerIntegrationFilter"]
    f2 --> f3["SecurityContextHolderFilter (loads SecurityContext from session or request attributes)"]
    f3 --> f4["HeaderWriterFilter (X-Frame-Options, HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options)"]
    f4 --> f5["CorsFilter (if CORS configured)"]
    f5 --> f6["CsrfFilter (validates CSRF token)"]
    f6 --> f7["LogoutFilter"]
    f7 --> f8["OAuth2AuthorizationRequestRedirectFilter / Saml2WebSsoAuthenticationRequestFilter"]
    f8 --> f9["UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter / BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter"]
    f9 --> f10["DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter / DefaultLogoutPageGeneratingFilter"]
    f10 --> f11["BasicAuthenticationFilter"]
    f11 --> f12["RequestCacheAwareFilter"]
    f12 --> f13["SecurityContextHolderAwareRequestFilter"]
    f13 --> f14["AnonymousAuthenticationFilter (anonymous principal if no auth yet)"]
    f14 --> f15["ExceptionTranslationFilter (catches AccessDenied / Authentication exceptions)"]
    f15 --> f16["AuthorizationFilter (replaces FilterSecurityInterceptor in 6.x)"]
    f16 --> ctl["DispatcherServlet -> @RestController"]
```

sections.title: Built-in Filters in Order (What Each Does)
sections.content:
**Boot-time setup:**
- `DelegatingFilterProxy` registered as the single servlet filter
- Delegates to `FilterChainProxy` bean
- `FilterChainProxy` holds the list of `SecurityFilterChain`s

**The chain (top to bottom):**
- **`DisableEncodeUrlFilter`** — security hardening (prevents session ID URL encoding)
- **`WebAsyncManagerIntegrationFilter`** — propagates `SecurityContext` for async dispatch
- **`SecurityContextHolderFilter`** — loads `SecurityContext` from session/request and clears at end
- **`HeaderWriterFilter`** — writes security headers (`X-Frame-Options`, HSTS, CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options`)
- **`CorsFilter`** — only if CORS configured via `http.cors(...)`
- **`CsrfFilter`** — validates CSRF token for state-changing requests
- **`LogoutFilter`** — handles `POST /logout`
- **`OAuth2AuthorizationRequestRedirectFilter` / `Saml2WebSsoAuthenticationRequestFilter`** — initiates OAuth2/SAML
- **`UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter` / `BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter`** — authenticates credentials/tokens
- **`DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter` / `DefaultLogoutPageGeneratingFilter`** — auto-render login/logout pages
- **`BasicAuthenticationFilter`** — HTTP Basic auth
- **`RequestCacheAwareFilter`** — replays original request after login
- **`SecurityContextHolderAwareRequestFilter`** — adapts `HttpServletRequest` (`isUserInRole`, `getPrincipal`)
- **`AnonymousAuthenticationFilter`** — sets anonymous principal if still unauthenticated
- **`ExceptionTranslationFilter`** — catches `AccessDeniedException` / `AuthenticationException` and translates to HTTP responses
- **`AuthorizationFilter`** — final access control check (replaced `FilterSecurityInterceptor` in 6.x)

sections.title: Spring Security 6 Configuration (Single Chain)
Multiple Filter Chains (Mixed Auth)
Custom Filters, UserDetailsService, AuthenticationManager
Configuration Patterns: Helps, Hurts, Watch For
sections.content:
**When multiple chains help:**
- API + web frontend in same app (different CSRF, session, auth)
- Actuator with separate auth (Basic for ops, JWT for app)
- Tenant-specific or version-specific security

**When single chain is enough:**
- Pure REST API (one auth strategy)
- Pure server-rendered MVC (one session-based auth)
- Avoid complexity until you actually need it

**When custom filters help:**
- API key auth alongside JWT
- Multi-tenancy (tenant resolution from subdomain/header)
- Pre-auth audit logging
- Custom request enrichment

**When custom filters hurt:**
- Re-implementing what Spring already does (`oauth2ResourceServer`, `formLogin`)
- Wrong position -> `SecurityContext` empty when authorization runs
- Catching auth exceptions in filter -> security bypass

**Watch for:**
- **Rule order** — `anyRequest().authenticated()` before specific `permitAll()` blocks everything
- **`hasRole("ADMIN")` vs `hasAuthority("ROLE_ADMIN")`** — `hasRole` auto-prefixes `ROLE_`
- **CSRF mixed across chains** — disabled on `/api/**` enabled on `/web/**` requires separate chains
- **Session created with STATELESS** if controllers call `request.getSession()`
- **Missing `@Order`** -> undefined chain evaluation
- **`X-Frame-Options: DENY`** blocks H2 console / iframe UIs in dev
- **Forgetting `@EnableMethodSecurity`** -> `@PreAuthorize` ignored silently
- **Mixing servlet + reactive** in one app — doesn't work
- **`DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter`** showing for API -> remove `formLogin()`
- **Custom filter at wrong position** — `addFilterBefore` vs `addFilterAt` semantics differ

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **Spring Security is a servlet filter chain** (`FilterChainProxy`) with many built-in filters in a fixed order.
- **`SecurityFilterChain` beans** replace `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` (removed in 6.0).
- **Multiple chains** for mixed auth (`/api/**` JWT, `/web/**` session); use **`@Order`**.
- **`requestMatchers`** replaces `antMatchers`; **`authorizeHttpRequests`** replaces `authorizeRequests`.
- **Rule order** — specific rules first, `anyRequest()` last.
- **`SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS`** for APIs; **enable CSRF** for cookie-based web apps.
- **Custom filters** via `addFilterBefore/After/At` at appropriate position.
- **Built-in headers** (CSP, HSTS, `X-Frame-Options`) — tune per app.
- **`@EnableMethodSecurity`** for `@PreAuthorize`/`@PostAuthorize`.
- **Test with `@WithMockUser`** and `mvc.perform(...).with(csrf())`.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**How it plugs in**
- Boot time: Spring registers `DelegatingFilterProxy`
- Delegates to `FilterChainProxy` bean holding `SecurityFilterChain` instances
- Each chain is a list of filters applied to requests matching a `SecurityMatcher`
- First matching chain wins; filters run in fixed order

**Key built-in filters in order**
- SecurityContextHolderFilter -> loads context
- HeaderWriterFilter -> security headers
- CorsFilter, CsrfFilter, LogoutFilter
- UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter / BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter
- BasicAuthenticationFilter, RequestCacheAwareFilter
- AnonymousAuthenticationFilter
- ExceptionTranslationFilter -> AuthorizationFilter (replaces FilterSecurityInterceptor)

**Spring Security 6 single-chain config**
- `@Configuration @EnableWebSecurity`
- `@Bean SecurityFilterChain` with `HttpSecurity`
- `csrf.disable()` for API; `csrf` enabled for browser
- `authorizeHttpRequests` + `requestMatchers`; `anyRequest().authenticated()` last
- `sessionCreationPolicy(STATELESS)` for tokens
- `oauth2ResourceServer.jwt(...)` for JWT

**Multiple chains**
- `@Order(1)` apiChain with `securityMatcher("/api/**")`
- `@Order(2)` webChain with `securityMatcher("/web/**", "/login")`
- `@Order(3)` actuatorChain with `securityMatcher("/actuator/**")`
- First matching `securityMatcher` wins

**Custom filter**
- Extend `OncePerRequestFilter`
- Set `Authentication` in `SecurityContextHolder`
- Register with `addFilterBefore(filter, UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter.class)`

**Migration checklist (pre-Boot 3 -> Boot 3+)**
- `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` -> `SecurityFilterChain` bean
- `antMatchers` -> `requestMatchers`
- `authorizeRequests` -> `authorizeHttpRequests`
- Remove `.and()` chaining; use lambda DSL
- `EnableGlobalMethodSecurity` -> `EnableMethodSecurity`

**Common gotchas**
- Rule order: specific first, anyRequest last
- `hasRole` vs `hasAuthority` (ROLE_ prefix)
- `STATELESS` broken by `request.getSession()` in controllers
- Missing `@Order` -> undefined evaluation
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY` blocks dev iframes (H2 console)
- `@EnableMethodSecurity` required for `@PreAuthorize`

questions.question: How do you migrate from WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter to the modern SecurityFilterChain config in Spring Security 6?
questions.title: WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter to SecurityFilterChain Migration (Spring Security 6)
questions.direct_answer: Spring Security 6 removed **`WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter`**. Migrate by replacing the adapter subclass with a **`SecurityFilterChain` bean** that takes `HttpSecurity` and returns `http.build()`. Replace **`configure(AuthenticationManagerBuilder)`** with a **`UserDetailsService`** + **`PasswordEncoder`** bean (and optionally a `DaoAuthenticationProvider`/`AuthenticationManager` bean). Replace **`configure(WebSecurity)`** ignore lists with `WebSecurityCustomizer`. Switch **`antMatchers`** -> **`requestMatchers`**, **`authorizeRequests`** -> **`authorizeHttpRequests`**, **`@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity`** -> **`@EnableMethodSecurity`**, and remove all **`.and()`** chaining in favor of the lambda DSL.

interviewer_intent.testing: Hands-on knowledge of the Spring Security 5.7 -> 6 migration that every Boot 3 upgrade hits.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Leaving `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` in code, mixing `.and()` with lambda DSL, or losing CSRF/role-prefix nuances during the rewrite.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss the `AuthorizationFilter` replacing `FilterSecurityInterceptor`, the new `authorizeHttpRequests` model, and `WebSecurityCustomizer` as the replacement for `configure(WebSecurity)`.

sections.title: Why the Migration: Component Model Over Inheritance
sections.content:
Spring Security 5.7 deprecated `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` and 6.0 removed it.
- The reason is architectural: **inheritance tied configuration to a single class**, prevented multiple configurations from coexisting cleanly, and made the API less Spring-idiomatic.
- The replacement is a **bean-based component model**: declare `SecurityFilterChain`, `UserDetailsService`, `PasswordEncoder`, and (optionally) `AuthenticationManager` as `@Bean`s and let Spring wire them.

**The migration touches four areas:**
- **`configure(HttpSecurity)`** -> `SecurityFilterChain` bean
- **`configure(AuthenticationManagerBuilder)`** -> `UserDetailsService` + `PasswordEncoder` (+ optional `AuthenticationManager` bean)
- **`configure(WebSecurity)`** -> `WebSecurityCustomizer` bean
- **DSL syntax** — `antMatchers` -> `requestMatchers`, `authorizeRequests` -> `authorizeHttpRequests`, lambda DSL replaces `.and()` chaining

Under the hood, **`AuthorizationFilter`** replaces **`FilterSecurityInterceptor`** as the final access control gate. The new `authorizeHttpRequests` model uses `AuthorizationManager<RequestAuthorizationContext>` — composable, type-safe, and easier to extend with reactive support.

sections.title: Before: Spring Security 5.x with WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter
After: Spring Security 6 with SecurityFilterChain Bean
Migration Mapping (Old API to New)
sections.content:
**Class structure:**
- `extends WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` -> remove inheritance, use `@Configuration` only
- `@Override configure(HttpSecurity)` -> `@Bean SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity)`
- `@Override configure(WebSecurity)` -> `@Bean WebSecurityCustomizer`
- `@Override configure(AuthenticationManagerBuilder)` -> `@Bean UserDetailsService` + `@Bean PasswordEncoder` (+ optional `AuthenticationManager`)

**DSL changes:**
- `antMatchers(...)` -> `requestMatchers(...)`
- `mvcMatchers(...)` -> `requestMatchers(...)` (now MVC-aware by default)
- `regexMatchers(...)` -> `RegexRequestMatcher.regexMatcher(...)`
- `authorizeRequests()` -> `authorizeHttpRequests()`
- `.and().csrf()` -> `.csrf(csrf -> ...)` lambda
- `.and().formLogin()` -> `.formLogin(form -> ...)` lambda
- `.and()` chaining -> remove entirely; each method takes a `Customizer` lambda

**Annotations:**
- `@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity(prePostEnabled = true)` -> `@EnableMethodSecurity` (prePost on by default)
- `@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity(securedEnabled = true)` -> `@EnableMethodSecurity(securedEnabled = true)`

**Disabling features:**
- `.csrf().disable()` -> `.csrf(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)` or `.csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable())`
- `.formLogin().disable()` -> `.formLogin(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)`

**`AuthenticationManager` access:**
- `authenticationManagerBean()` from adapter -> declare your own `@Bean AuthenticationManager`
- For programmatic auth in custom filters/controllers, inject the bean directly

sections.title: Multiple Chains and Method Security in the New Model
Old vs New API: At-a-Glance Mapping
sections.content:
**Quick reference for the most common migration touchpoints:**

| Old (5.x) | New (6.x) |
|---|---|
| `extends WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` | `@Configuration` class only |
| `configure(HttpSecurity)` | `@Bean SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity)` |
| `configure(WebSecurity)` | `@Bean WebSecurityCustomizer` |
| `configure(AuthenticationManagerBuilder)` | `@Bean UserDetailsService` + `@Bean PasswordEncoder` |
| `authenticationManagerBean()` | `@Bean AuthenticationManager` |
| `antMatchers(...)` | `requestMatchers(...)` |
| `authorizeRequests()` | `authorizeHttpRequests()` |
| `.and().formLogin()...` | `.formLogin(form -> ...)` |
| `.csrf().disable()` | `.csrf(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)` |
| `@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity(prePostEnabled = true)` | `@EnableMethodSecurity` |
| `FilterSecurityInterceptor` | `AuthorizationFilter` |
| `AccessDecisionManager` | `AuthorizationManager<T>` |

sections.title: Migration: Helps, Hurts, Watch For
sections.content:
**When the new model helps:**
- Multiple `SecurityFilterChain` beans for mixed auth
- Cleaner test setup — beans, not subclasses
- Reactive parity (`SecurityWebFilterChain` mirrors the API)
- Easier to compose with `@Profile`, `@Conditional`
- `AuthorizationManager` API is composable and extensible

**When migration hurts:**
- Mixed `.and()` and lambda DSL during incremental migration -> compile errors
- Forgetting `@EnableMethodSecurity` -> annotations silently ignored
- Losing the `_csrf` token name change with new request handler -> CSRF failures
- `mvcMatchers` -> `requestMatchers` semantics: now MVC-aware automatically; some path matching differences
- `WebSecurityCustomizer` ignore-lists bypass ALL Spring Security filters — never use for `/api/**`

**Watch for:**
- **`hasRole("ADMIN")`** still requires `ROLE_ADMIN` authorities — the prefix convention didn't change
- **`AuthenticationManager` not auto-wired** — you must declare it explicitly
- **`@Autowired UserDetailsService`** now works because it's a bean (was previously inside the adapter)
- **`http.exceptionHandling()`** lambda — must set `authenticationEntryPoint` and `accessDeniedHandler` explicitly for APIs
- **CSRF token request handler change** — `XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler` is the new default; SPAs may need `CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler` for plain XOR-free tokens
- **`requestMatchers("/admin/**")`** ambiguity — when both servlet and MVC are present, may need `RequestMatcher` instances explicitly
- **`PathPatternRequestMatcher` (6.5+)** — newer matcher type; use for fine-grained MVC-aware matching

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **`WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` removed in 6.0** — replace with `SecurityFilterChain` bean.
- **`configure(HttpSecurity)` -> `@Bean SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity)`** returning `http.build()`.
- **`configure(WebSecurity)` -> `@Bean WebSecurityCustomizer`** for filter-chain bypass (static resources only).
- **`configure(AuthenticationManagerBuilder)` -> `@Bean UserDetailsService` + `@Bean PasswordEncoder`** (+ optional `AuthenticationManager`).
- **`antMatchers` -> `requestMatchers`**, **`authorizeRequests` -> `authorizeHttpRequests`**, **`.and()` -> lambda DSL**.
- **`@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity` -> `@EnableMethodSecurity`** (prePost on by default).
- **`AuthorizationFilter` replaces `FilterSecurityInterceptor`** under the hood.
- **Never use `WebSecurityCustomizer` for `/api/**`** — it bypasses ALL security filters.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**The structural change**
- `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` removed in 6.0
- Replace inheritance with `@Bean` declarations: `SecurityFilterChain`, `UserDetailsService`, `PasswordEncoder`, `AuthenticationManager`
- `configure(WebSecurity)` -> `WebSecurityCustomizer` bean

**DSL changes**
- `antMatchers` -> `requestMatchers`
- `authorizeRequests` -> `authorizeHttpRequests`
- Remove `.and()` chaining; each method takes a lambda Customizer
- `.csrf().disable()` -> `.csrf(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)`

**Annotation changes**
- `@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity(prePostEnabled = true)` -> `@EnableMethodSecurity` (prePost on by default)
- `securedEnabled` / `jsr250Enabled` still explicit

**AuthenticationManager**
- No more `authenticationManagerBean()`
- Declare `@Bean AuthenticationManager` with `DaoAuthenticationProvider` + `ProviderManager`

**Internal change**
- `AuthorizationFilter` replaces `FilterSecurityInterceptor`
- New `AuthorizationManager<RequestAuthorizationContext>` API — composable, extensible

**Watch for**
- Mixing `.and()` with lambda DSL -> compile errors
- Forgetting `@EnableMethodSecurity` -> `@PreAuthorize` ignored
- `hasRole("ADMIN")` still requires `ROLE_ADMIN` authority prefix
- `WebSecurityCustomizer` only for static resources — never for API paths
- CSRF token handler change: `XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler` may break SPAs that expect plain tokens
